relevant_rules.details: It matched the malicious sysmon.service creation and, in the primary window, the benign lab-sysmon-sensor.service creation used to preserve telemetry. It sees PATH CREATE under systemd directories but not unit content, ExecStart, package ownership, or the security-product mismatch.
relevant_rules.precision: Useful generic precursor with material administrative noise; correlate with parsed unit content and execution.

relevant_rules.details: The rule detects cp /bin/sh .../crond, not a security-named systemd unit. It is a useful masquerading precedent but does not cover sysmon.service.
The rule keys on known operator/tool image names. Adaptix is absent and the generated agent ran renamed, so filename additions would remain evadable.

dns_linux_coverage.conclusion: SigmaHQ master has no Linux DNS-tunneling or DoH behavior rule relevant to this flow.
dns_linux_coverage.what_local_rules_add: Zeek and Suricata coverage for the fixed session/operation/sequence/index/Base32 query structure, independent of implant name, resolver, port, and parent domain. The rules are explicitly source-plus-listener validated because a Linux DNS agent could not be generated.
